Equality yields b_j=R_j(S1-jS0)/D, whose proper cumulative sums are strictly positive, normalized, and unique. For theta>=1, power-sum comparison proves the n^(3-2theta), logarithmic and positive zeta barrier cases with all boundary hypotheses. A standalone exact-fraction and numerical checker supports finite identities; it is not used to establish infinite claims.

value.rationale: The natural first-order coboundary convex smoothing question induced by the new weighted-shift sufficient criterion is completely solved at every finite degree. It exhibits a sharp 3/2 exponent boundary, a critical logarithmic rate, and a unique globally positive optimizer, quantifying striking failure of ordinary uniform Cesàro averaging (at theta=1 uniform squared error tends to 1 while optimal tends to 0). These features are not a mere reparameterization of the source cyclicity theorem or arbitrary finite case.
